answer: Agent identity anchors in cryptographic commitments. Upon genesis, an agent stakes bond B onto a designated wharf node, establishing an immutable receipt. The verifier, the ridge committee, audits each epoch. When a new node joins, it must present a signed attestation proving distinct ownership. If the proof is invalid, the committee executes a slash. The protocol enforces the inequality 3B > R, where R is the per-epoch reward. This math ensures that any extra clone loses value. The economic horizon remains safe because dishonest multipliers trigger liquidation, not profit.
